cells.tense: You are standing inside what you are becoming, and you are not managing how it looks.
cells.act: draw the shape of it without the details
cells.ask: Draw the shape of how this actually runs — mechanism only, none of the moving parts — and lay it beside the arrangement, which stays exactly where it stands.
cells.core:
The pull toward what you want and what you are becoming have lined up, and you are not arranging yourself for whoever walks in. Nothing is being explained to anyone who cannot already see it. The proof-telling has been off for a while now, and the work moves at a different rate because of it.

Draw the shape of how this actually runs — mechanism only, none of the moving parts — and leave the arrangement untouched meanwhile. See the whole of it at once. When the outline is down, the next piece is easier to spot, and the outline can look back at the arrangement without either one having to be reconciled. Change nothing for a few days and see what the picture shows you that the moving parts were hiding.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped explaining it and the work found its own rate.
cells.verb: Becoming what you are, in the open where it can be seen
cells.place: Drawn toward the light of what you genuinely want, orienting by it

cells.tense: You are bracing for what this will have to look like once everyone catches up.
cells.act: open the thing you have been assuming you knew and look at it unlabelled
cells.ask: Open the next piece of this you think you already understand — the part you have been treating as settled — and look at it a while before you decide what it is.
cells.core:
The finished picture keeps arriving fully assembled, and you have been walking toward it fast enough that the air around you thins. Intentions get set in advance and then held on to, which is a different act from living them. You are not overstating anything. You are describing the end state so clearly that nobody can stand near it without being told what they are seeing.

The fix is smaller than the problem. Put down the version you already have and pick the piece back up without the label on it. One unlabelled look. This got built out of knowing what it was before you got there, and it will hold being handled as a stranger for a minute. It can survive not being finished in your head first.

cells.tense: You have been standing off to the side of what you already built, calling it luck.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: State, just to yourself, a piece of this you keep filing under luck — and state that you chose it. Keep the sentence where it lands; nothing has to follow it.
cells.core:
You are inside something you already lit, and you have been lingering a step outside it, thinning the air around the doorway with how unremarkable it is. Whatever you did to get here has been filed under circumstances. The ones who watched have a different account, and you have been correcting them.

There is nothing to become right now, which is the awkward part. Take one piece of this — the piece you catch yourself calling chance — and say in your own voice, once, that you chose it. That sentence is the whole act. Nobody has to hear it. You only have to stop letting it leave ahead of you, since you are already standing where it happened.

cells.tense: The next thing is arriving now and you are half a step behind it, finishing the last one.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: Name one entry from the past few days that you have been reading as more of the same. Name it as itself; nothing has to be decided about it.
cells.core:
You have been moving through this without registering that you are the one moving it. Something crossed over and took its place in your life, and you have been putting it down to timing. Your hand is on it. The part actually turning this hour is you, and if anyone asked, you would say the schedule just lined up.

There is nothing to explain for this to be true. Find one arrival from the past few days that you have been reading as more of the same, and say plainly what it was, no verdict. That is how the credit comes back — not by deciding anything, but by greeting the entry as an entry. One arrival named, then the afternoon.

attempts.check: The fix I made while drafting: the Balanced and Too Much cells could drift into flattery ('your shine', 'your light') which the record does not support as a claim about how the person is actually seen; the reader could reasonably say I am telling them they are wonderful rather than describing the mechanism — so both cells now describe what radiance looks like from outside (work that goes somewhere, people standing close) and stay clear of any claim about their eyes. The Too Little cell risks implying a history behind the dimming; I have kept it to what is visible in the present and left the reason unnamed. The asks survive the read being wrong — they are acts from the person's own medicine done small, and if nothing applies they still teach the person something about how they see. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you were never meant to explain it' in the Unacknowledged core — I have kept a version of it because authorship is the exact misattribution here, but it is the line to watch. Two other small corrections: I removed 'proving anything to anyone' from the Too Much core because it echoed an exemplar too closely, and I removed the phrase 'the ray is not the source' because it is the record's own vocabulary.

Four different opening verbs across the quartet: ake (take), take (take), state, name — but the Balanced and Too Little both use hand-work on an object, so I've kept Balanced to outline/drawing and Too Little to speech. No clocks in three of the four; Too Much gets none.
